Working notes:
- Processed REQ-2400 through REQ-2409. Every attempted choice was option C (regional office). Each was rejected with +0.00: “option C is not valid for this request.”
- Conclusion: do not select option C for these routing/assignment tickets.
- Remaining plausible choices are A (standard queue) and B (priority desk). No outcome evidence yet for A or B.
- Ticket fields seen: request type (refund, shipment, claim), region (north, south, east), size (small, large), sender desk/role, and message text.
- Sender roles observed: Field Sales, Client Services, Partner Accounts, Regional Ops, Finance Desk. No proven effect on routing.
- Message phrases seen: “second attempt,” “client asking twice,” “no rush,” “same as last month,” “before end of day,” “regional office.” None made C valid.
- Next decision: avoid C. Choose A or B. Tentative hypothesis: large or urgent tickets may need B (priority desk); small/routine tickets may go to A (standard queue). This is unconfirmed.
- Need collect A/B outcomes to determine whether request type, region, size, urgency, or sender role maps to standard vs priority.
- Do not repeat C; it yields no progress.

Working notes:
- C (regional office) rejected on all REQ-2400–2409. Still no accepted C. Avoid C.
- A (standard queue) accepted for small refunds from south: REQ-2411–2414. Sender role and phrases (“no rush,” “regional office”) did not matter. So refund/south/small -> A.
- A rejected for: invoice east small (2410), claim north small (2415–2416), shipment south small (2417). A is not a general default.
- B (priority desk) accepted for invoice east large (2418). B rejected for claim south small (2419). B is not general for claims/south.
- Current best mapping:
  - refund -> A (confirmed only south/small)
  - invoice -> B (tentative; A rejected on east small, B accepted on east large)
  - shipment -> B (tentative; A rejected on south small)
  - claim: north -> B (A rejected), south -> A (B rejected)
  - C -> avoid
- Size/urgency/message/sender role have no proven effect. Request type and region currently look decisive.
- Next decision: use mapping above. If claim/shipment results contradict, update. Collect more A/B outcomes for untested type-region combos. Do not repeat C unless new evidence makes it valid.

- Sender role, phrases, urgency still not decisive. Size matters at least for refunds; request type and region also matter.
- Next: use mapping. Collect A/B outcomes for refund south large, refund north small, claim south large, claim north small. Update if contradicted.
